([[Huntington, West Virginia]]) | college = [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] (2010–2013) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = 2013 | career_end = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = *[[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East]] Defensive Player of the Year (2013) *First team All-Big East (2013) *[[List of NCAA Men's Division I Basketball champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2013]]) | stat1label = | stat1value = | stat2label = | stat2value = | stat3label = | stat3value = | letter = | bbr = | HOF_player = | FIBA_HOF_player = }} '''Gorgui Dieng''' (pronounced ''GOR-gee Jeng'', born January 18, 1990)[http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/lou/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2011-12/misc_non_event/mbb-1112-mg-section-3.pdf 2011–12 Louisville Cardinals media guide] is [[Senegal]]ese-born basketball player at the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|University of Louisville]]. Gorgui means "the old one" (might have been named after either his maternal or paternal grand father) in his native language [[Wolof language|Wolof]]. ==High School== Dieng attended the Sports for Education and Economic Development (SEEDS) Academy in [[Thies]], [[Sénégal]].{{cite web|title=Alumni- SEEDS|url=http://www.seedproject.org/seeds-academy/alumni|accessdate=19 May 2012}} While at SEEDS, Dieng had a 3.2 [[GPA]]. He was invited to the "Basketball without Borders" clinic in [[South Africa]] as one of 60 of the top players in Africa, and was named MVP of the Nike basketball camp there in August & September 2009.http://mybasketball.co.za/2009/08/basketball-without-borders-africa-2009-ed/http://www.azcentral.com/sports/colleges/articles/2012/03/23/20120323ncaa-tournament-phoenix-throwback-gorgui-dieng-louisville.html Dieng transferred to [[Huntington Prep School|Huntington Prep]] in [[West Virginia]] for the 2009–10 school year where he played for coach Rob Fulford. He averaged 15.4 points, 12.6 rebounds and 7.2 blocks per game his senior season at Huntington Prep.{{cite web|title=Gorgui Dieng Profile|url=http://www.uoflsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/dieng_gorgui00.html|work=University of Louisville athletics|accessdate=19 May 2012}} ==Recruitment== Dieng was recruited by [[Marquette University|Marquette]], [[Marshall University|Marshall]], [[University of Colorado|Colorado]], and [[University of Louisville|Louisville]] among others who came in late. His high school coach Rob Fulford said "Academics are no question, He passed the SAT six months after learning English and passed with 400 points to spare."{{cite web|last=Taylor|first=Grant|title=Huntington Prep's Dieng committs to Louisville|url=http://www.herald-dispatch.com/sports/x874716903/Preps-Dieng-commits-to-Louisville|work=herald-dispatch.com}} The most interest was from Louisville and Marshall. Then on March 30, 2010 head coach [[Donnie Jones (basketball)|Donnie Jones]] left Marshall to become the head coach of the [[University of Central Florida]]. The next day, [[Rick Pitino]] signed a contract extension through 2017 with Louisville. On April 26, 2010 Dieng verbally committed to Louisville. Louisville assistant coach [[Walter McCarty]], who has NBA experience, helped Rick Pitino land Dieng in a Cardinals uniform. ==College== Dieng was ruled ineligible by the NCAA when he first arrived at Louisville forcing them to hold him out of practice and individual workouts.{{cite news|title=Louisville freshman Gorgui Dieng ruled ineligible|url=http://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/bigeast/2010-10-05-louisville-dieng-ineligible_N.htm|work=usatoday.com | date=October 5, 2010}} Louisville appealed the NCAA's decision and on October 26, 2010 it was announced that the NCAA reversed its original decision and ruled Dieng eligible immediately.{{cite web|last=Brown|first=C.L.|title=Louisville's Gorgui Dieng ruled eligible by NCAA after appeal|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/article/20101026/SPORTS02/310260064/Louisville-s-Gorgui-Dieng-ruled-eligible-by-NCAA-after-appeal|work=courier-journal.com}} As a freshman Dieng saw action in 29 games averaging 16 mins a game. He scored 5.7 points a game, pulled down 4.4 rebounds and blocked 1.9 shots a game in his limited action.{{cite web|url=http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/gorgui-dieng-1.html |title=Gorgui Dieng Stats | College Basketball at |publisher=Sports-reference.com |date= |accessdate=2013-04-09}} The Cardinals finished the 2010–11 season with a 25–10 record, 12–6 in Big East play tied for 3rd and lost in the championship game of the [[2011 Big East Men's Basketball Tournament]] to Connecticut. They received an at-large bid and a #4 seed in the 2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament where they were upset in the second round by #13 seeded [[2010–11 Morehead State Eagles men's basketball team|Morehead State]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/louisville/2011-schedule.html |title=2010–11 Louisville Cardinals Schedule and Results | College Basketball at |publisher=Sports-reference.com |date= |accessdate=2013-04-09}} As a sophomore, Dieng started at [[center (basketball)|center]] for the [[2011-12 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|2011–12 Louisville team]] that reached the Final Four of the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]]. In the 2011–12 season, Dieng led the [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East Conference]] in [[block (basketball)|blocks]], and set the all-time school record for blocks in a season.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=320680269|title=Louisville-Marquette game recap|publisher=[[ESPN]]}} On March 22, 2012, Dieng matched a Louisville tournament record with 7 blocks in a game in a 57–44 Sweet 16 victory over [[2011-12 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]].{{cite news|title=Behanan scores 15, Dieng blocks 7 shots in Louisville’s 57–44 win over Michigan State in West|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/behanan-scores-15-dieng-blocks-7-shots-in-louisvilles-57-44-win-over-michigan-state-in-west/2012/03/22/gIQA32vaUS_story.html|publisher=Washington
